//: Committed defaults, meant to run out of the box against the development database
in docker-compose.yml. That database has to exist first:
docker compose up -d db
dotnet ef database update --project src/SancMeld.Core
The connection string below is throwaway: user sancmeld, password sancmeld, on
port 55432, all of which are already published in docker-compose.yml. It is a
convenience default, not a credential.
NEVER edit it to hold a real one. A password that reaches a tracked file is in the
history for good, and this project's predecessor shipped exactly that. Point at
your own server from outside the repository instead:
development  -> dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:SancMeld" "..."
docker/prod  -> environment variable ConnectionStrings__SancMeld=...
local file   -> appsettings.Development.json (git-ignored)
Each of those overrides this file, so nothing here has to be deleted first.
Sanctions sources are NOT configured here: they live in the sanctions_source
table so imports, snapshots and designations can reference them by key.
EntityFrameworkCore is pinned to Warning on purpose. An import issues tens of
thousands of statements; at Information, EF logs every one of them, burying the
few lines that say what the import did under megabytes of SQL.
Note that every key under Logging:LogLevel is read as a category name and every
value as a level, so a comment cannot live inside that section.
